lessons.title: Percentage change, compound interest and growth and decay
lessons.summary: Use multipliers to increase and decrease by a percentage, calculate percentage change, find original amounts in reverse percentage problems, and model repeated change with compound interest, growth and decay.
objectives: I can use a decimal multiplier to increase or decrease an amount by a percentage.
I can calculate a percentage change, profit or loss.
I can find an original amount after a percentage change (reverse percentages).
I can calculate compound interest and other repeated percentage changes using a multiplier to a power.
I can solve growth and decay problems, including depreciation.

activities.title: Multipliers
activities.content:
## One number does the whole job

A **multiplier** is the decimal you multiply by to make a percentage change in a single step.

- To **increase** by 12%: the new amount is $100\% + 12\% = 112\%$, so multiply by **1.12**.
- To **decrease** by 12%: the new amount is $100\% - 12\% = 88\%$, so multiply by **0.88**.

| Change | Multiplier |
|---|---|
| increase by 5% | 1.05 |
| increase by 40% | 1.4 |
| increase by 2.5% | 1.025 |
| decrease by 30% | 0.7 |
| decrease by 8% | 0.92 |
| decrease by 0.5% | 0.995 |

**A jacket costs £64. In a sale it is reduced by 35%. Find the sale price.**

$64 \times 0.65 = £41.60$

**A salary of £28 000 rises by 3%. Find the new salary.**

$28\,000 \times 1.03 = £28\,840$

## Why multipliers matter

They are quicker than finding the percentage and adding, they are essential for repeated changes (compound interest), and they make reverse problems a single division. Get comfortable converting any percentage change into its multiplier instantly.

A quick check: an increase gives a multiplier **above 1**; a decrease gives one **below 1**.

question.text: Write down the multiplier for a decrease of 15%.
A phone costs £340. Its price increases by 7.5%. Work out the new price in pounds.

activities.title: Percentage change and reverse percentages
activities.content:
## Percentage change

$\text{percentage change} = \dfrac{\text{change}}{\text{original}} \times 100$

The **original** value always goes on the bottom, never the new one.

**A house bought for £180 000 sells for £207 000.**

Change $= 27\,000$. Percentage profit $= \dfrac{27\,000}{180\,000} \times 100 = 15\%$.

**A car bought for £9 000 is sold for £7 200.**

Change $= 1\,800$. Percentage loss $= \dfrac{1\,800}{9\,000} \times 100 = 20\%$.

## Reverse percentages: finding the original

When you are told the amount **after** a change and asked for the amount **before**, divide by the multiplier.

**A coat costs £51 after a 15% reduction. What was the original price?**

The sale price is 85% of the original, so

$\text{original} = 51 \div 0.85 = £60$

Check: $60 \times 0.85 = 51$ ✓.

**A bill of £96 includes VAT at 20%. What was the bill before VAT?**

$96 \div 1.2 = £80$.

The classic trap is to take 15% off £51 or 20% off £96. That gives the wrong answer because the percentage was of the *original* amount, not of the new one. Always ask: "What percentage of the original is this amount?" and divide by that as a decimal.

question.text: A shop buys a lamp for £45 and sells it for £63. Work out the percentage profit.
After a 12% pay rise, Mia earns £30 240 a year. What was her salary before the rise, in pounds?
question.hint: £30 240 is 112% of the original. Divide by 1.12.

activities.title: Worked example: compound interest
activities.content:
## Interest on the interest

With **simple interest** the same amount is added every year. With **compound interest** each year's interest is calculated on the new, larger balance, so the amount grows faster.

The formula:

$\text{final amount} = \text{initial amount} \times (\text{multiplier})^{\text{number of years}}$

**£2 500 is invested at 4% compound interest per year. Find the value after 3 years.**

Multiplier for 4% growth $= 1.04$.

$2\,500 \times 1.04^3 = 2\,500 \times 1.124864 = £2\,812.16$

Year by year it would be £2 600, then £2 704, then £2 812.16, and the power does all three steps at once.

**How much interest was earned?** $2\,812.16 - 2\,500 = £312.16$. Read the question: "total amount" and "interest earned" are different answers.

**Compare with simple interest:** 4% of £2 500 is £100 per year, so 3 years gives £300. Compound earns £12.16 more.

## Finding the number of years

**How many years until £2 500 at 4% first exceeds £3 000?**

Try powers: $1.04^4 = 1.1699$ gives £2 924.65; $1.04^5 = 1.2167$ gives £3 041.63. So **5 years**. Use trial and improvement with the power button on your calculator.

question.text: £4 000 is invested at 2.5% compound interest per year. Work out the value of the investment after 4 years, to the nearest penny.

activities.title: Growth and decay
activities.content:
## The same idea everywhere

Any quantity that changes by a **fixed percentage each period** follows the same rule as compound interest:

$\text{new value} = \text{start value} \times (\text{multiplier})^n$

- **Growth** (population, bacteria, prices): multiplier above 1.
- **Decay** (depreciation, radioactive decay, cooling): multiplier below 1.

**Depreciation.** A van bought for £24 000 loses 18% of its value each year. Its value after 3 years:

$24\,000 \times 0.82^3 = 24\,000 \times 0.551368 = £13\,232.83$

**Population growth.** A town of 15 000 people grows by 6% a year. After 5 years:

$15\,000 \times 1.06^5 = 15\,000 \times 1.3382 = 20\,073$ (nearest whole person).

## Mixed rates

If the rate changes, multiply by each multiplier in turn. An account paying 3% for the first year and 2% for the next two years:

$\text{start} \times 1.03 \times 1.02^2$

## Finding the rate

A population grows from 800 to 968 in 2 years at a fixed rate. Then $800 \times m^2 = 968$, so $m^2 = 1.21$ and $m = 1.1$: a rate of **10%** per year.

## A useful fact

A 20% decrease followed by a 20% increase does **not** return you to the start: $0.8 \times 1.2 = 0.96$, a 4% overall loss.

question.text: A laptop is bought for £850. Its value falls by 20% each year. Work out its value after 3 years, in pounds.
Match each situation to the calculation that solves it.
question.hint: Increase means multiplier above 1; reverse problems divide.
question.explanation: Increase £200 by 5% for 3 years: $200 \times 1.05^3$. Decrease £200 by 5% once: $200 \times 0.95$. Original amount before 5% increase to £200: $200 \div 1.05$. Original before 5% decrease to £200: $200 \div 0.95$.

activities.title: Common mistakes
activities.content:
## Watch out for

- **Wrong multiplier.** A 4% increase is × 1.04, not × 1.4. A 4% decrease is × 0.96, not × 0.4.
- **Reverse percentages.** Divide by the multiplier; never take the percentage off the new amount.
- **Percentage change.** Divide by the **original** value.
- **Compound vs simple.** Compound uses a power; simple interest adds the same amount each year.
- **Answering the wrong question.** "Interest earned" means subtract the starting amount; "total amount" means do not.
- **Rounding mid-calculation.** Keep $1.04^3$ in the calculator; round only the final money answer to 2 d.p.
- **Assuming changes cancel.** Down 20% then up 20% is not back to the start.
- **Number of periods.** Interest "per month" for 2 years is 24 periods.

question.text:
Aisha invests £6 000 in an account paying 3% compound interest per year.

(a) Work out the value of the investment after 2 years.

(b) Aisha's brother invests a sum of money at the same rate. After 1 year his investment is worth £4 635. How much did he invest?

(c) Aisha says her investment will double in less than 20 years. Show whether she is correct.
question.explanation: (a) $6\,000 \times 1.0609 = £6\,365.40$. (b) $4\,635 \div 1.03 = £4\,500$. (c) $1.03^{20} = 1.806$, so after 20 years the investment is $6\,000 \times 1.806 = £10\,836$, which is less than £12 000. She is not correct (doubling takes about 24 years).

markScheme.criterion: Uses multiplier 1.03 squared (or two steps of 3%)
Concludes she is not correct as the value is less than £12 000 (not doubled)

activities.title: Key points
activities.content:
- Increase by $p\%$: multiply by $1 + \frac{p}{100}$. Decrease: multiply by $1 - \frac{p}{100}$.
- Percentage change $= \frac{\text{change}}{\text{original}} \times 100$.
- Reverse percentage: **divide** by the multiplier to get back to the original.
- Repeated change: $\text{final} = \text{start} \times \text{multiplier}^n$; this covers compound interest, growth and decay/depreciation.
- Interest earned = final − start. Round money only at the end.
- Percentage changes do not simply cancel out or add up; multiply the multipliers.

practiceQuestions.text: Write down the multiplier for an increase of 6%.
A pair of trainers costs £72. In a sale the price is reduced by 25%. Work out the sale price in pounds.
A bicycle bought for £250 is sold for £190. Work out the percentage loss.
A TV costs £480 including VAT at 20%. Which calculation gives the price before VAT?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The price with VAT is 1.2 × the original, so the original is $480 \div 1.2 = £400$.

options.feedback: Taking 20% off the *new* price gives £384, which is wrong; the 20% was of the original.

practiceQuestions.text: The number of members of a club fell by 8% to 322. How many members were there before the fall?
£1 500 is invested at 5% compound interest per year. How much **interest** is earned in 3 years? Give your answer to the nearest penny.
practiceQuestions.hint: Find the total first: $1\,500 \times 1.05^3$. Then subtract £1 500.

practiceQuestions.text: True or false: if a price is increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%, it returns to its original value.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False. $100 \times 1.1 = 110$, then $110 \times 0.9 = 99$. Overall a 1% decrease, because $1.1 \times 0.9 = 0.99$.

practiceQuestions.text: A car is bought for £18 000 and depreciates by 15% each year. Work out its value after 4 years, to the nearest pound.
A bacteria colony doubles in size every hour. It starts with 500 bacteria. After how many whole hours does the colony first exceed 20 000 bacteria?
Tom says: "£2 000 at 5% compound interest for 2 years earns £200 interest." Explain the mistake Tom has made and give the correct amount of interest.
practiceQuestions.hint: In the second year, interest is earned on more than £2 000.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Tom has calculated simple interest (£100 each year). With compound interest the second year's interest is 5% of £2 100, which is £105. Total interest $= 2\,000 \times 1.05^2 - 2\,000 = £205$.

markScheme.criterion: Explains that Tom used simple interest / did not pay interest on the interest

practiceQuestions.text:
The population of a village was 2 400 in 2020. It increased by 5% in 2021 and by 8% in 2022.

(a) Work out the population at the end of 2022.

(b) Work out the overall percentage increase from 2020 to the end of 2022.
practiceQuestions.hint: (a) Multiply by 1.05 then by 1.08. (b) Multiply the two multipliers together, or use (change ÷ original) × 100.
practiceQuestions.explanation: (a) $2\,400 \times 1.05 \times 1.08 = 2\,721.6$, so 2 722 people (or 2 721). (b) $1.05 \times 1.08 = 1.134$, an overall increase of 13.4%.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies by 1.05 and 1.08 (or equivalent two-step working)

practiceQuestions.text: Write down the multiplier for a decrease of 32%.
practiceQuestions.hint: $100\% - 32\%$, then write the percentage as a decimal.

practiceQuestions.hint: £943 is 115% of the original rent. Divide by 1.15.

practiceQuestions.text:
Ravi invests £8 000 in an account paying 2.5% compound interest per year.

(a) Work out the value of the investment after 2 years.

(b) Ravi's sister invests a sum of money at the same rate. After 1 year her investment is worth £5 125. How much did she invest?

(c) Ravi says his investment will be worth more than £10 000 after 10 years. Show whether he is correct.
practiceQuestions.hint: (a) $8\,000 \times 1.025^2$. (b) Divide by 1.025. (c) Work out $8\,000 \times 1.025^{10}$ and compare with £10 000.

markScheme.criterion: Uses multiplier 1.025 squared (or two steps of 2.5%)
Concludes he is correct as the value is more than £10 000
